paper_design_summary: A model-only simulation with no human participants. The authors run closed loops in which SDXL generates an image from a text prompt, LLaVA describes the image in 50 words or fewer, and the description becomes the next prompt: 700 trajectories (100 novelty-search start prompts x 7 LLaVA temperatures, 100 iterations each), and a second experiment that crosses 4 image generators with 4 captioning models (the first 40 start prompts, 100 steps each). Semantic drift and convergence are measured with cosine distances between all-MiniLM-L6-v2 embeddings of the prompts and with k-means clustering of the final prompts.

studies.label: Temperature experiment: SDXL-LLaVA loops at seven LLaVA sampling temperatures

assignment.what_was_assigned: No people were assigned. Each of the 100 novelty-search start prompts seeded one trajectory at each of seven LLaVA sampling temperatures (0.1, 0.3, 0.5, 0.7, 0.9, 1.1, 1.3), giving 700 trajectories. The same start prompts were used at every temperature.
assignment.quote: For each temperature condition, 100 independent trajectories were run using the diverse initial prompts generated through novelty search, yielding 700 total trajectories.
assignment.locator: PDF p. 11 (printed p. 10), Methods, Iterative language-image loop construction

participants.who: No human participants. The units are 700 model-generated trajectories (100 start prompts x 7 temperatures), each run for 100 prompt-image-prompt cycles.
participants.quote: experiments were conducted across seven temperature values: 0.1, 0.3, 0.5, 0.7, 0.9, 1.1, and 1.3. Each trajectory evolved through 100 prompt-image-prompt cycles.
participants.locator: PDF p. 11 (printed p. 10), Methods, Iterative language-image loop construction

ai_tool.name_model: Stable Diffusion XL (SDXL) for image generation and LLaVA (llava:13b from ollama.com) for image description. Start prompts were generated by LLaMA 3.2 at temperature 0.9, and all-MiniLM-L6-v2 sentence embeddings were used for measurement only. The paper names no SDXL checkpoint for this experiment.
ai_tool.how_used: No person used AI. SDXL draws a 512 x 512 image from the current prompt (50 inference steps, CFG scale 7.5), LLaVA describes it in 50 words or fewer, and the description becomes the next prompt.

task.description: Autonomous loop: generate an image from the prompt, describe the image in vivid, artistic terms in 50 words or fewer, and use the description as the next prompt.

eligibility.reason: Both experiments are model_only. The paper describes models that "interact without human input" (PDF p. 2, printed p. 1, The bigger picture). No people were assigned to AI assistance: conditions vary sampling temperatures or generator-captioner combinations across model trajectories (PDF p. 11, printed p. 10, Methods, Iterative language-image loop construction; PDF p. 6, printed p. 5, Results, Other models). There is no human participant sample; the reported trajectories and start prompts are not people. Scored drift and clustering concern model-generated prompt embeddings, not outputs produced by participants (PDF p. 11, printed p. 10, Methods, Embedding analysis and cosine similarity; PDF p. 4, printed p. 3, Results, Temperature-specific and pooled clustering analysis). All three criteria are therefore not_met. The discussion of prior human cultural-transmission studies does not contribute a human experiment or reanalysis here. No human-output comparison or observational human corpus qualifies the paper as context evidence. Under codebook section 3, model-only studies remain in the screening report and are omitted from the dataset.

one_line_finding: In 700 autonomous SDXL-LLaVA loops of 100 iterations, the pooled final prompts formed k = 12 clusters (per-temperature k of 14 to 19 in the Figure 5 legend, given as 15 to 20 in the text), and in the 4 x 4 generator-captioner experiment the captioning model accounted for about 13.6 percent of the variance in step-to-step drift against 0.2 percent for the image generator (PDF p. 4; Figure 5, PDF p. 8; PDF p. 6; Table 1, PDF p. 11).
notes: The paper runs two experiments, entered here as S1 and S2; both screeners entered one combined study. PDF page = printed page + 1, because PDF p. 1 is a highlights cover page. The current markdown conversion was read in full through the references; it includes the Conclusion, Limitations, Methods, Table 1, and back matter. All 13 PDF pages were also read, Table 1 was recovered with PDF table extraction, and the Figure 5 legend was independently checked in a rendered PDF crop. No c008 challenge files were present. There were no pre-existing open questions or unresolved reconciliation differences; the paper reporting inconsistencies recorded below are carried as non-eligibility open items. There are no human participants, so arms and outcomes are empty. Machine-only results, none bearing on the three questions: novelty search raised the k-NN dispersion of the start prompts from 0.63 to 0.75, and overall dispersion reached 0.90 (PDF p. 3). S1: cumulative cosine distance from the initial prompt stabilizes around 0.85 at temperatures 0.1-0.3 and approaches 0.87 at 1.1-1.3 (PDF p. 4 text; Figure 3A, PDF p. 6). Step-to-step cosine distance is around 0.22 at higher and 0.13 at lower temperatures, stable after about 20 iterations (PDF p. 4; Figure 3B, PDF p. 6). The k-means elbow analysis gives k = 12 for the 700 pooled final prompts, and the Figure 5 legend gives k_opt = 16, 18, 19, 14, 16, 17, 17 for t = 0.1, 0.3, 0.5, 0.7, 0.9, 1.1, 1.3 (PDF p. 8, read from a zoomed render of the figure). S2: two-way ANOVA on the cosine distance between consecutive embeddings (Table 1, PDF p. 11): image generator (A) SS 0.0149, df 3, F 0.534, p 0.659; language model (B) SS 0.9247, df 3, F 33.242, p < 10^-19; A x B SS 0.0520, df 9, F 0.623, p 0.778; residual SS 5.786, df 624. Eta-squared is about 13.6 percent for the language model, 0.2 percent for the image generator, and 0.8 percent for the interaction (PDF p. 6). Inconsistencies inside the paper: the text, the Figure 5 caption, and the Discussion give per-temperature optimal k as 15 to 20 (PDF p. 4, p. 8, p. 6), while the legend values run from 14 to 19. The text's 'k = 17 for T = 0.1– 1.3' (PDF p. 4) contradicts 'k = 16 for T = 0.1' in the same sentence. The Figure 3 caption describes the shaded areas both as the standard error across 100 trajectories and as 95 percent confidence intervals (PDF p. 6). The initial image (step = 0) was skipped when analyzing trajectories (PDF p. 11, printed p. 10, Methods, Embedding analysis and cosine similarity); this is an exclusion of a machine-generated trajectory step, not of people.
